::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 17th 1890  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Girton College Cambridge, Yonge IV 19
:::

Dear [Mr Innes](people/person_744.qmd)
I am very sorry to see [Miss Cheape](people/person_289.qmd)’s proof did not reach her. You told me about a month ago that she had sent a fresh address but as I had sent her the proof of [Mr Valentine](other_books/otherbook_630.qmd) full a month before  - (or rather I knew it had been sent) I did not suppose it applied   People <u>never</u> forward proofs, they always take them for advertisements.

By the by today’s post brings me a complaint of this [advertisement](organizations/other_217.qmd) <u>fastened</u> into the [Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd) - I am afraid there is no escaping what to me is an absolute nuisance, and if other people were like me would be a detriment to the sale of things so obtruded.

The [Newbery magazine](organizations/other_83.qmd) writes to ask for my biography - I answer that I have always set my face against publishing people’s lives when they are alive, and that I decline decidedly.

I think I had better write to [Miss Gaye](people/person_552.qmd) that not being proprietor, my editorial engagements must always be subject to the arrangements of the publisher, so that the new plan throws me out.

I do not know if it is personal feeling but I had rather make the [Cameos](cmy_books/cmybook_240.qmd) shorter than leave them out alternately. I know (for instance) that they are the one thing the [Dean of Lincoln](people/person_244.qmd) always reads.

However, it is impossible to please everybody. I thought the call was for more, not fewer miscellaneous articles

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

**Note:** W.J. Butler.
